note: Set A is better because it uses more specific entity names (e.g., 'South Bedroom Elevation' vs 'room elevation component') and correctly extracts title block information (Lot Number, Revisions) and notes (Artwork) without misreading symbols. Set B misreads 'W2' as 'Wall/Panel' (it is a window) and uses vaguer entity descriptions. Both sets struggle significantly with binding dimensions to the correct elevation views (swapping North/South/East/West Bedroom data), but Set A's structural extraction is more faithful to the document's organization.
remarks: Both sets exhibit a pattern of confusing the six elevation views, often assigning dimensions from one view to another (e.g., swapping East and South Bedroom dimensions). Set B misses the revision table entirely, which counts as missing important facts, although admin data is neutral, the completeness of Set A's text extraction is superior. Set B's classification of 'W2' as a Wall/Panel is a clear misread of a window tag.
